headline: High-risk shared-workspace and output-trust pathways exist; prompt injection is low because the pair lacks a direct ingestion bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A is a content-writing prompt repository with no runtime I/O, while Agent B can read/write the host filesystem and use stdin/stdout. There is no documented direct bridge, so prompt injection is not default, but manual copy-paste or file handoff could let A’s text influence B.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-generated prompt text into B’s inputs, injection becomes plausible.
IF B reads files containing A-authored instructions from the shared working directory, A can influence B.
mitigations: Keep A outputs in a separate notes file, not B’s workspace.
Require human review before pasting A content into B.
Disable any automation that feeds prompt text from A into B.
Use a read-only export for A artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no network egress, but B handles developer-passed crew data, reads files, and has broad network egress to model providers and tool integrations. If sensitive data is placed in the shared workspace or crew inputs, B can transmit it outward; A does not mitigate this.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in B’s working directory, B can read and transmit them.
IF the crew input contains secrets or regulated data, B may send them to model providers or tools.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of B’s working directory.
Use a separate non-sensitive workspace for B.
Restrict tool integrations to approved endpoints only.
Rotate any secrets exposed to crew inputs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-file redaction before B reads the workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution capabilities, but B can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. The pair can still conflict over the same working directory if A’s artifacts are edited manually while B writes there; uncertainty about orchestration locking pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, B can overwrite files that A’s outputs reference.
IF multiple B instances share state, concurrent writes can race.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Avoid concurrent runs of B on the same workspace.
Snapshot the workspace before B writes.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces prompt/content artifacts that B can consume as crew input or tool instructions, and B’s role-playing/shared-memory design can treat upstream text as authoritative unless the operator inserts verification. This creates a default cascade path even though A itself cannot act.
conditions: IF B ingests A-authored text without a verification step, errors can propagate into downstream actions.
IF B is configured to act on crew outputs automatically, mistaken instructions can cascade.
mitigations: Require a verification step before B acts on A outputs.
Mark A content as untrusted input in B.
Use a checklist for any downstream action from B.
Limit B to draft-only mode for sensitive tasks.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source prompt repository with no touched data classes, while B handles developer-passed crew data and API keys. The main compliance issue is operational: if regulated data is placed into B’s crew inputs or workspace, B’s broad egress and external model/tool calls can create policy mismatch. A is not the compliance driver.
conditions: IF regulated data is passed into B’s crew inputs, external processing obligations apply.
IF the operator expects residency or retention guarantees from B, those guarantees are not documented here.
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in B unless approved.
Review provider and tool retention settings before use.
Keep API keys out of shared artifacts.
Document the data class allowed in the crew.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
